headline: LLM-guided search reports lower Toffoli and qubit costs across reversible quantum-circuit tasks
summary: A preprint introduces an evolutionary search in which LLMs propose reversible circuits and an evaluator scores them. Across seven of eight specified tasks, the authors report lower Toffoli and peak live-qubit counts than the listed baselines; the eighth presents a prime-field modular-inversion design using divsteps without a single prior reversible baseline. The linked author repository documents exact resource counting and randomized correctness tests, and two relied-on results have Lean proofs. These are bounded author-reported circuit results under task-specific contracts and error budgets, not independent reproduction, hardware performance, or end-to-end quantum advantage.
